question: In which part of the neurons, is the first electrical impulse created?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Dendrite**__.
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__
 
__ 

• **Dendrites** are the branch-like extensions of a neuron that receive signals from other neurons or external stimuli. The first electrical impulse is generated here when the dendrites detect a stimulus. 

• These impulses are the result of the movement of ions across the neuronal membrane, which creates an electrical signal known as an **action potential**. 

• The dendrites play a crucial role in the **initial phase of signal transmission**, where they collect and process incoming signals before relaying them to the cell body. 

• The electrical signals collected by the dendrites are transmitted to the **axon hillock**, where the decision to generate a full-fledged action potential is made. 

• The dendritic structure ensures that neurons can process multiple incoming signals simultaneously, enabling complex neurological functions. 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 
 

• **Structure of a Neuron:** 
 

• A neuron consists of three main parts: **dendrites**, a **cell body**, and an **axon**. 

• The **dendrites** receive signals, the **cell body** processes them, and the **axon** transmits the signals to the next neuron or target tissue. 
 
 

• **Role of Dendrites in Signal Transmission:** 
 

• Dendrites primarily function as **receivers of chemical or electrical signals** from other neurons or sensory organs. 

• The signals received are converted into small electrical changes called **graded potentials**, which travel toward the cell body. 
 
 

• **Action Potential:** 
 

• The electrical impulse in a neuron is called an **action potential**, a rapid change in electrical charge across the membrane that allows signals to travel along the neuron. 

• Action potentials are initiated only if the signals received by the dendrites and cell body reach a certain threshold at the **axon hillock**. 
 
 

• **Functions of Neuronal Components:** 
 

• **Cell Body (Soma):** Contains the nucleus and organelles; integrates incoming signals. 

• **Axon:** Conducts electrical impulses away from the cell body to other neurons or muscles. 

• **Nerve Endings:** Release neurotransmitters to communicate with other cells. 
 
 

• **Examples of Neuron Types:** 
 

• **Motor Neurons:** Carry signals from the central nervous system to muscles. 

• **Sensory Neurons:** Transmit sensory information like touch, heat, and pain to the brain. 

• **Interneurons:** Facilitate communication between sensory and motor neurons.
